text:
tim_acme: Hey — customer (acct: ACME-42) just flagged an invoice with ~7,200 tokens billed but console shows ~3,600 for the same date range. They say no heavy usage spikes. Can someone help triage? Invoice: https://invoices.internal/acme/INV-2026-03-15

emma_support: Thanks, filing here. Do we have the request ids / sample request traces from the invoice window? Any retention mismatch between metering and billing pipelines? :thinking:

tim_acme: I grabbed two example request IDs from the customer: req_8f3a2c and req_8f3a2d. They see the requests succeed client-side but the dashboard only shows one token cost per pair. Invoice seems to count both.

emma_support: Pasting the logs I can access from the billing ingestion for those IDs:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z ingest: received req_8f3a2c tokens=182
2026-03-15T10:12:35Z ingest: received req_8f3a2d tokens=178
2026-03-15T10:12:36Z billing: enqueue req_8f3a2c
2026-03-15T10:12:36Z billing: enqueue req_8f3a2d
```
emma_support: Dashboard query for ACME-42 around the same time shows only req_8f3a2c present (tokens=182). Dashboard trace link: https://console.internal/traces?trace=req_8f3a2c

raj_billing: Confirming — ledger shows two separate charge events for that minute. So billing pipeline has both entries. Dashboard aggregation (real-time) is missing one of them. Could be a deduping/visibility lag or a missed reconciliation.

lia_eng_infra: Quick hypothesis: I pulled edge proxy logs for that host — I'm seeing a pair of near-identical inbound POSTs within 400ms: one returned 502 to the client (proxy->upstream), then client retried and got 200. But I also see the X-Idempotency header is present only on the second request in some sessions. Looks like token refresh flow might strip headers on retry. Example (simplified):
```
Inbound 10.0.1.5 POST /v1/generate  X-Idempotency: none   -> proxied -> 502
Inbound 10.0.1.5 POST /v1/generate  X-Idempotency: abc123 -> proxied -> 200
```
lia_eng_infra: If billing ingestion is keyed by request body and not by idempotency header, both attempts could be recorded as separate usages. Alternatively, billing may be keyed by an internal request id from the gateway — if gateway assigns different ids across the 502/reauth path we'll see duplicates.

emma_support: That fits customer notes: they saw client success but invoice has an extra token charge. Any evidence of header stripping during auth refresh?

lia_eng_infra: Yes — on sessions where the client token expired we see a 401 returned, client-side code reauths and resends, but our proxy's reauth handler replaces the original X-Idempotency header (it was in a different header prefix). On a few hosts the handler drops unknown headers during the internal 401->reauth hop.

emma_support: Can you grab the raw proxy request ids for the two attempts? We can map them to billing ingestion IDs.

lia_eng_infra: Sent to thread: proxy-ids: gw-ff12 & gw-ff13. gw-ff12 (502) -> body hash abcdef -> gw-ff13 (200) -> body hash abcdef. Billing ingestion currently indexes by (ingest_timestamp, body_hash) but our dedupe window is 0s for cross-process duplicates. Two separate enqueue events were recorded.

raj_billing: Right now the billing pipeline dedupe needs a stronger key: prefer X-Idempotency when present, else body_hash + short time window. But because the header was missing on one attempt, dedupe failed. For retro billing corrections we can run a dedupe job for the affected accounts/time window.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: edge-proxy patch to preserve X-Idempotency during internal auth flow (canary to 2 hosts) — ETA 3h.

lia_eng_infra: I'll open a GH PR that: 1) ensures proxy copies idempotency header to internal reauth requests, 2) normalizes header prefix, 3) logs when header is dropped. Repro steps attached below.

emma_support: Repro steps for infra to validate (from internal QA):
1) Start session with a short-lived token (curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <expiring>" -H "X-Idempotency: abc123" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://edge.internal/v1/generate)
2) Force upstream to return 502 on first attempt (qa-proxy fault injection): iptables DROP or inject 502 rule
3) Observe two inbound attempts at proxy. Check final propagated headers to billing-ingest.

cURL example:
```
TOKEN=$(get-temp-token --ttl 2s)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Idempotency: abc123" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' https://edge.internal/v1/generate
# then watch proxy logs
```

emma_support: Proposed immediate customer remediation: 1) run dedupe job for ACME-42 over 2026-03-15 09:00-11:00 to collapse duplicates based on body_hash + 1s window where request bodies match, 2) offer invoice credit for confirmed duplicates, 3) notify customers of planned patch. Agree?

raj_billing: Agreed. I'll kick off the dedupe job and prepare a provisional credit. Need final confirmation list from lia (which proxy-ids map to ledger entries).

lia_eng_infra: I'll produce mapping report in next 60m and attach to the ticket. The canary patch will be out after code review; if canary looks good we'll roll to prod in 6h.

tim_acme: Appreciate the quick triage. Customer asked whether we can avoid manual credits going forward — will the patch prevent this class of duplicates?

lia_eng_infra: Yes — patch prevents header loss on reauth and adds a short dedupe buffer in the billing enqueue. Combined fix should stop these duplicate charges for auth-refresh related retries. We'll follow up with a postmortem if we find additional root causes.

emma_support: Action items:
- lia: mapping report + PR (#3421) -> 60m
- deploy-bot / infra: canary patch -> 3h
- raj: run dedupe job + provisional credit note -> start now, update in 2h
- emma: email customer + confirm credit policy wording -> 1h

tim_acme: Thanks, leaving contact if you need example logs: tim@acme.example.com

emma_support: Noted. I'll update thread when dedupe job finishes. :white_check_mark:
